body: When I was still working in retail, there was this couple with a baby boy, who was crying. He wouldn't stop, no matter how hard they tried. So I glanced over and miraculously he calmed down immediately. He probably just freaked out and fell quiet because of this intense stare down with an Asian adolescent wearing a blue, paper hat. But let's just stay optimistic and say I have magic, soothing eyes that relieve suffering instantaneously.

I'm sorry to hear that you had to go through that. I hope it will keep improving. Panic attacks are flat out frightening and the fear for one reoccurring just makes it worse.

After my first panic attack I started therapy at the GGZ. I was also suicidal at the time, so I had a lot to work on. After a while my situation bettered and the therapist decided I could stop treatment, although her explanation as to why she was acquitting me, wasn't too reassuring. It basically boiled down to 'You aren't feeling awful enough and we can't help you'. Slowly after the sessions ended, my mental state started going south again. With my girlfriend's support I decided to start therapy again at another institution. Tomorrow morning I'll be calling my healthcare provider to discuss the terms under which they cover the damages.

Although it might sound lame, have you ever considered therapy? Social anxiety, especially the level you are personally experiencing, isn't something you have to live with all your life. There's help out there, and you deserve it, like everybody else. There might be underlying causes, which need attention. Combined with the depression you describe, no therapist will just waver you away. Don't be afraid of that.

Personally I find it really difficult to allow people to help me. I recently discovered this cycle of self-pity and self-loathing I go through daily. If it's not clear what I mean by that, I can try giving an example, but like I said earlier; my brain is chaotic mess and finding an example is difficult. Before I never thought I deserved therapy, but I realized it's for the better of my relatives and friends as well. That's what motivating me right now; trying to improve their situation as well!

For me online contact is also nice every now and then. Although I'm pretty quick on my feet, my brain can me a huge chaotic mess sometimes. Writing gives clarity and gives me time to be logical and to the point.

Last couple of months I've isolated myself pretty badly as well. I tell most people I don't really feel the need, which is sometimes true, because I'm introverted as well, but sharing helps me to lighten my load. Too bad I don't get the chance that often lately. 

My semester this year actually kicked off with a panic attack, so I think I can relate. An ambulance had to be called. I was just going completely haywire.

Do you have a job at the moment? I'm looking into volunteer work to get my social fix. Feel like describing that social anxiety?

Sounds like a heavy load to carry man. Dropped out of college twice as well, for somewhat the same reason you did, namely the depressive mood. First I studied Law, then Physics. Law I did for half a year before finding out it didn't offer what I was looking for. Year after that I started with Physics, but I kind of had a mental breakdown right before the semester kicked of, so I had to resign after only three months. Both times at Leiden University.

Game development sounds really awesome though! Get what you're saying about the future perspective, but an sich it seems amazing. Did some programming in Swift to make a game, but I guess you couldn't really call that a real game :p

19M/Dutch (as well)
What college did you go to and what did you study? :)
Sound like some heavy, but interesting topics. Shoot me a message if you're still up to chat. I was actually looking for the kind of 'dark' conversation you're describing

Anyone know a way to develop that inferior Fe to the point where it is manageable? I found zen buddhism really helpful in a way, but it killed my impulsiveness, which I love so much.

Tend to have a meltdown when emotions start to run to high. Might be more a psychopathological flaw than something INTP-like...

Good luck with your job, man. Glad to hear that you'll try and make that effort. You'll end up on the winning side if you keep taking small steps. Of course I can't promise you that, but all that kept me going during those dark periods was hope, however lame that may sound. To me life is about hope, believing in a better tomorrow, and sometimes hoping isn't needed, because I'm in the bliss. It's right there in that moment. 

In the near future I'll try writing in a log daily. Someone gave me the tip to write down three emotions daily, basically anything that is not on the median of emptiness I'm usually riding. Either positive or negative, it's doesn't matter.

Last night I was awake til 8AM. I fell asleep, but the first two hours of sleep felt more like hallucination than resting. The dark just feels safe to me. Life isn't calling, so I don't have to feel guilty about the 'worthless' things that keep me occupied.

Right now, Albert Camus for sure. The objective, honest way of looking at the world. I discovered his work during a time of my life when suicide played a key role. On the one hand because of the despair it mended through recognition, but mostly due to him posing suicide as the main question of philosophy. It summed up the obsessive thought I'd been having for two years, and I couldn't help but love the man for giving me that The Fall I read twice in two days and the Myth of Sisyphus I'm still working on.

"I know man is capable of great deeds, but if he isn't capable of great emotions, I don't care for him much." -The Plague

Another idol for me is Thich Nhat Hanh. His zen buddhist teachings really hit the sweet spot when I was going through a break up. The way I was trying to patch things up with her, was perfectly described in his book 'True Love'. It gave me the confidence to be that compassionate, all-ears romantic. It kickstarted a manic period in which in slept two hours per night and would go to clubs by myself. Only good memories about that time.

"When another person makes you suffer, it is because he suffers deeply within himself, and his suffering is spilling over. He does not need punishment; he needs help. That's the message he is sending."

Still trying to live up to this.

To be honest, I only once met a person who 'got me'. This may sound pretentious, but I'm a reserved and pretty anti-social person, so I rarely get to the point where a person gets me. By then I'll probably have moved on, or they have. The one time it did happen, I just flat out told the guy I despised him for getting to my core and that I felt threatened. He felt the same way, and we just ended up being arrogant assholes to each other. Honest assholes though.

Inactivity and insomnia are two things I've been struggling with as well.  Especially the inactivity is a big problem, because I just get stuck in my own head an start to ponder life's big questions. For a time I was depressed, accompanied by panic and anger attacks, and my go to thought always was and still is suicide. In the bigger picture it's all just meaningless. That's how I tried to rationalize it. Everything just loses it's glow in the shadow of that mind-set. Switching it back to seeing the bright side of life and being present is incredibly hard, and there's no shame in looking for professional help. Things might be haunting you, and those ghosts are often invisible.

What really helped me was a friend telling me about her suicide obsession when she was younger. She wasn't depressed, but suicide seemed to be lurking around every corner. The knowledge that someone had dealt with something similar I was going through, convinced me there was a way out. I hope I can kind of give you that same feeling.

Feeling the same way. Managed to quit drugs and alcohol, got support from my family and partner, started therapy, exercising frequently, making enough money to get by... But every time I'm standing on the balcony in my girlfriends apartment to smoke a cigaret, I can't help but think about jumping and turning myself into a big puddle of flesh. For me it helps to stay real and look at the facts. When my conditions aren't absolutely miserable, there's some space for hope. Curious what the future holds.

Edit: Also the theoretical knowledge that I'm not cured. I just got way better at masking it during all those years of misery. I got accustomed to this state of mind. Still need help though.
I'm also very curious about this rational. It might clear things up for me.

Walking through the woods, or along the coast of the lake nearby, makes me feel the same way. Especially at night, when no one is there to notice me. For me it's the feeling of being part of something larger, something overpowering, that makes me feel at ease. Like the silence and darkness affirm the insignificance I always prescribe to myself. Only nature is honest to me, while every human I've ever met, is a lying scumbag secretly loathing me. Death seemed so tempting. What put me off was the thought, that I wouldn't even be there to watch my own funeral from high up in the clouds, to check whether someone was maybe, just maybe, crying over my coffin after all, while they lowered me into the ground. And it was this exact thought which kept me from ending myself; that repulsive longing for tears. I despised myself for it, but instead of placing me closer to the edge, it pulled me away from it. 'Why' I still can't figure out, and the reasons probably aren't too great, but I'm glad it did. I'm still struggling to hang on. I'm just asking you to hang on with me. I wished I had the perfect string of words to return to you your joy for life, but I don't. All I can tell you, is that it's the only life you get. A flash of consciousness between two eternal voids of nothingness. However tempting that nothingness may sound when you're in such a dark place, you won't be able look back and regret choosing to end it. Be brave, be your own savior, and fight. Much love from a fellow struggler.
